description: AI HOST EPISODE: format 'host_episode' = one presenter talking to camera, the camera changing every piece (frontal, three-quarter, close), the same host and set throughout, native voice, 16:9. It returns a 480p DRAFT; HD (720p) is a SEPARATE call with `fromDraft` (quote it with dryRun, run it only when the user asks). Otherwise: turn a TOPIC into a finished narrated explainer video, in one of TWO LANES (`lane`). BURNED ON-SCREEN TEXT IS OFF BY DEFAULT; the film ships clean unless the user asks; `captions:true` adds held key points and `subtitles:true` adds subtitles timed to the narration. Takes SEVERAL minutes — one image render per frame; NOT for a short product ad: use render_ad, generate_video or make_template_ad. Full rules: get_instructions({topic:'make_explainer'}).

aspectRatio.description: '9:16' default (a faceless channel video and a host episode default to 16:9)

brandName.description: brand name for the end card — omit to leave it unbranded

cameras.description: host_episode: the rotation, ids frontal / three_quarter / close or framings in words; one entry = one fixed camera

captions.description: turn ON-SCREEN TEXT on. DEFAULT FALSE, and leave it false unless the user asks — the narration already says the point and the pictures carry it, so the clean film is the better default. `captions:true` on its own burns SUBTITLES (see below), because that is what a caption is for: showing what is being said when the phone is on mute. Slim white text (CAPS in the stills lane), thin black outline, bottom safe band, no plate, no box.

channel.description: the CHANNEL TYPE — it sets the pacing, the narration register and the default look, and is orthogonal to `style` (a named style always wins): explainer (casual second-person, fast cuts), history (witty chronological retelling / documentary), kids (fastest, question-first, warm teacher), fairytale (slow, atmospheric myth or folklore). Default 'explainer'.

creator.description: host_episode: the host, a saved creator or a preset by name or id (list_creators)

dryRun.description: true = return the estimated credits this explainer reserves (its own pricing, stopped at the hold) and render nothing. Quote it before running one; try frameDensity lean or minimal when the balance is short.

endCard.description: append the branded end card. DEFAULT FALSE — set true ONLY when the user asks for one

expected_credits.description: the get_cost price; refused unbilled if the live price differs

format.description: blocks lane: 'explainer' (default; Gemini Omni 720p, 16:9 or 9:16, runs exactly the length asked) or 'faceless_channel' (a YouTube/TikTok faceless channel video; MiniMax H3 at 2K, 16:9 by default, five hard cuts per 10s block, runs exactly the length asked: a last part-block is rendered whole and cut). Omit and a history / kids / fairytale channel is a faceless channel video. 'host_episode' = the AI host episode (see the top).

frameDensity.description: how many pictures per second of narration, and therefore what it costs. 'standard' (default) is a frame about every 1.5s — the density a stills film needs to read as a film rather than a slideshow; 'lean' is one about every 2.5s (the longest hold that still reads as a film, ~40% of the frames and ~40% of the cost); 'minimal' is one picture about every 3.5s, the cheapest and the longest any still is ever held, and it reads close to a slideshow. Only drop below the default if the user asked for something cheaper.

fromDraft.description: host_episode: a finished draft's job id, to render it in HD (720p) with the same script, cameras, set and host

fromFilm.description: A PRESENTER ON A FINISHED FILM (only when the user asks for one): the job id of a finished video-blocks explainer or faceless-channel film. With `presenter`, that film comes back with a presenter speaking each block's line on screen; every block keeps its own picture and the film without the presenter is kept (cleanVideo). Never add a presenter unasked.

get_cost.description: true: return the price only; nothing runs or bills

hostImage.description: host_episode: a photo URL of the host instead (upload_file for a local file); a real person's face needs a paid plan

idempotency_key.description: chosen once, resent unchanged on retries: the same key never buys twice

lane.description: 'blocks' (default) = 10-second video blocks, real motion, one narrated line per block; 'stills' = the picture film (a still about every 1.5s, narrated, no video model; cheaper). Quote either with dryRun.

music.description: music bed under the narration, measured to sit about 14 dB under the voice and sidechain-ducked beneath it. Omit and the KIDS and FAIRYTALE channels get their recommended bed COMPOSED for this film — those two are the only channels a bed is due on unasked, and it costs a small flat fee; every other channel ships dry. 'off' forces silence. 'library' takes a free curated track only, and ships dry when none is on file. NAME A MOOD (upbeat / calm / warm / epic / tense / playful / elegant / hype / chill / dramatic) or DESCRIBE it in words to compose one on ANY channel, at the same fee. hermoso_capabilities reports the exact figure as explainerMusicCredits; quote it before you turn a bed on or pick a mood.

presenter.description: with fromFilm: who presents and how. A face the video model flags stops it, nothing charged, with the choices to offer.

creator.description: a saved creator or a preset, by name or id (list_creators)

image.description: or a photo / avatar of the presenter (upload_file for a local file); a real person's face follows the real-face rules

look.description: 'corner' (default): cut out of a green screen, standing in a bottom corner; 'badge': a round badge in a corner; 'split': the block on one half, the presenter on the other

position.description: 'br' (default), 'bl', 'tr' or 'tl' (a corner cutout stays at the bottom); for split, 'bl' puts the presenter first

scale.description: the share of the frame the presenter takes, 0.2-0.8 (default: the look's own size)

voice.description: a voice to re-voice the presenter to, only when the user names one (default: the presenter's own voice from the video model)

script.description: host_episode: the exact words, said verbatim and split at natural breaks into 4-30s pieces

setting.description: host_episode: the set in words (default: written to fit the topic)

style.description: visual style: 'cinematic' (default, photoreal); styled shortcuts editorial_collage, flat_vector, stickman, whiteboard, ink_marker, silhouette, storybook, paper_diorama, isometric, claymation, pixel_art, watercolor, fluffy_toy, low_poly, stylized_3d, studio_3d (the Kids default), mannequin; or ANY look described in words ('80s anime cel animation'), locked across every frame. Ask rather than pick silently; a styled look costs more.

subtitles.description: which on-screen text, once `captions` is on. LEAVE IT UNSET (or true) for SUBTITLES — every spoken word, in order, timed to the narration; no extra render, and there is NO cue limit, so the whole film is subtitled however long it runs (at most 4 words and one line a cue; 5 words / 32 characters in stills). Set it FALSE only if the user explicitly wants section HEADINGS instead: one short summary label held over each ~7-15s section. That is NOT what is being said — it is a label about it — so it is the wrong answer to "add captions" and to anyone watching on mute. `subtitles:true` also implies `captions:true`. TIMING: in the default blocks lane each cue is timed to its own spoken words (one listen to the narration, inside the quote; per-block timing, said, if it fails). In the stills lane cues are spread over each section’s measured narration by character count, exact at section edges, a few tenths off within one: it is not a word-level speech clock, so never promise frame-accurate sync there.

thumbnail.description: host_episode: one thumbnail of the host (default true)

topic.description: what the explainer should teach or explain — a topic or a short brief (host_episode: or pass `script`)

upscale.description: optional FINAL upscale — 2 doubles each side, 4 quadruples. Captions and the end card are burned BEFORE it so they upscale with the frame. It is priced BY LENGTH and it is the expensive part — several times the cost of rendering the film itself. hermoso_capabilities reports the exact figures per length as explainerUpscaleCredits. Never turn it on unasked: quote the number and let the user choose.

voice.description: narration voice name — omit for the default warm read
